_readme: THE SOURCE REGISTRY. One entry per data source, carrying the endpoint a reader would
have to hit and the EXACT filter values applied to it. It exists because an audit on
2026-08-17 found only 3 of 20 datasets published a source URL and none published its
industry or program codes — so the artifacts asserted reproducibility they did not
provide. A methodology box that names 'BLS QCEW' without naming NAICS 3252 tells a
reader where to start and not what was done.
Every value below was extracted from the fetch scripts, not written from memory.
`script` is the file that hits the endpoint; run it and you get the same bytes.
`by_artifact` maps each published page to the sources it rests on, so PV.methodology()
can render the right subset without every derive script having to declare it. Adding a
page here is how it gets a reproduce block; tools/verify.mjs fails a page that has none.
PUBLIC CUT. This registry lists only the sources behind the analyses published in
this repository. The internal series has more pages and more sources; their
absence here is stated in the README rather than left to be discovered.

qcew.name: BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages

filters.NAICS codes: 10 (all industries), 31-33 (manufacturing), 325 (chemical manufacturing), 3252 (resin, synthetic rubber and fibers), 3255 (paint, coating and adhesive), 326 (plastics and rubber products), 3261 (plastics products), 3262 (rubber products)
filters.geography: county FIPS, PIC-12 and NEO-14 (see footprints.py)
filters.note: PIC’s own measurement register is 3252 + 3255 + 326. NAICS 325 is context, not cluster: it contains pharmaceuticals and agricultural chemicals.
filters.provenance_page: fetch_provenance.py re-uses this source for one pull: 2016 annual, own_code 5, industry 326+32521+325991 at agglvl 55/57/58 — the QCEW instrument comparison on the provenance page

qwi.name: Census Quarterly Workforce Indicators, seasonally adjusted

filters.industry: 326 (plastics and rubber products manufacturing); 00 (all industries) as the benchmark on the talent demand chart
filters.note: EarnBeg is average monthly earnings of employees who also worked for the same employer in the prior quarter — stable jobs, not new hires.

filters.segment: JT00 — all jobs, all sectors. LODES origin-destination carries NO industry dimension, so this is the whole economy and never the polymer cluster.
filters.files: main (both ends in state) plus aux (work in state, home out of state). Omitting aux makes the region look artificially self-contained.
filters.geography: work end bounded to PIC-12 for the commute matrix; home end bounded to PIC-12 for the reciprocal; peer comparison reads twelve states' main files
filters.note: Both ends are employer-reported addresses. The home end is a residence on file, not evidence anyone travelled.

ipeds.name: IPEDS Completions, via the Urban Institute Education Data API
ipeds.agency: National Center for Education Statistics, served by the Urban Institute

filters.CIP-6 core: 143201 (polymer/plastics engineering), 400507 (polymer chemistry), 150607 (plastics and polymer engineering technology)
filters.CIP-6 adjacent: 141801 (materials engineering), 400510 (materials chemistry), 401001 (materials science), 141901 (mechanical engineering), 140701 (chemical engineering), 400501 (chemistry general), 151701 (energy systems technology)
filters.majornum: 1 only, so a double major is counted once
filters.race/sex: race=99 and sex=99 are the total rows; race=8 is nonresident alien. The two partitions are aggregated separately and never crossed — this endpoint does not offer the cross-tab at CIP-6.
filters.national benchmark: the same codes with no state filter, restricted to codes the footprint itself confers as a programme — which excludes 150607, since PIC-12's entire history in it is two awards from one community college in one year
filters.note: Two earlier code entries did not exist and silently returned zero: 140320 (a transposition of 143201) and 143101 (materials science is in the 40 series, not 14). A core code returning zero across every year and institution is evidence of a bad code, not of no graduates.
filters.ipeds_cip: fetch_ipeds_cip.py adds institution × CIP × year (used by talent and occupations)

filters.dataset: Regional, RPP by metropolitan statistical area
filters.base: a fixed national basket, US average = 100
filters.note: Published at METRO, which neither nests inside nor tiles PIC-12. Akron, Cleveland-Elyria and Youngstown-Warren each include territory the footprint excludes. Do not sum the three and call it PIC-12.

fred.name: FRED producer price and commodity series
fred.agency: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

filters.series: WPU072 (PPI rubber and plastic products), WPU066 (PPI plastics resins and materials), WPU06 (PPI industrial chemicals), PCU326326 (PPI plastics and rubber products manufacturing), PCU325211325211 (PPI plastics material and resin manufacturing), WTISPLC (WTI crude oil spot)
filters.note: Producer price indexes, not consumer prices. Index levels, not dollars.
filters.run order: fetch_rest.py FIRST, then fetch_chain_prices.py. The second appends the feedstock and resin links to fred.json; running fetch_rest.py after it overwrites the file and silently drops them.

oews.name: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, metropolitan file

filters.geography: metropolitan area — same non-nesting caveat as BEA RPP
filters.note: One year only. This is a level, not a trend; the wage trend on the talent page comes from QWI instead.

usaspending.name: USAspending federal contract and grant obligations

filters.NAICS: 325* and 326* manufacturing codes only, so university and research awards are invisible by construction — a university files under 61xxxx
filters.geography: place of performance, a reported field on the award rather than an observation of where work happened
filters.note: Obligations are money legally committed, not cash spent.

filters.compiled: Merged from eight internal and public record sets — operational status reports, funding and award files, verified deck facts, and primary-press dates from the quote bank. 487 raw rows reduced to 104 dated events.
filters.publicOnly: Only events recorded as PUBLIC appear. Internal operational milestones, and the record of which dates slipped, are deliberately excluded — this is the public record, not the project's whole history.
filters.forward_are_hollow: 18 of the 104 are future milestones and are drawn hollow, so a plan never reads as a fact.
filters.not_reproducible: Hand-compiled from documents rather than fetched from an API. Every event carries its own date and organisation; there is no script that regenerates this file, and pretending otherwise would be the opposite of what this registry is for.

heritage_register.name: NEO Polymer Wins register — heritage and discoveries collections
heritage_register.agency: Polymer Industry Cluster (internal register; only PROVEN rows and public sources travel)

filters.proven_only: Only rows the register's INDEX labels PROVEN are emitted; the 5 CLAIMED rows are withheld as id + label + year only, with no wording.
filters.collections: heritage (what changed the region's capacity) and discoveries (what was first understood here). The shipped, licensed, living and pic-era collections are a different tense and are not on this page.
filters.sources_travel: Only http(s) URLs and bibliographic lines travel; vault-path source references are stripped at build and counted (3).
filters.do_not_say_guard: Every emitted sentence is checked against the register's own do-not-say list; a hit fails the build.
filters.wartime_tonnage: Four different measures exist in the sources and none is printed — the register's standing rule.
filters.reproducibility: The register is internal; the builder (PIC-decks/tools/build-heritage-web.py) cannot be re-run from a public clone. The emitted data/heritage.json IS the published artifact, like the operating record; every row carries its public source URLs so each can be checked by hand.

oews_national.name: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, national file

filters.occupations: the SOC set read from oews.json (26 codes) — the metro pull defines the set
filters.dedupe: 51-2090 appears as broad and detailed with identical values; one row kept, detailed preferred
filters.note: all industries; '#' ceiling ($115/hr, $239,200/yr) and '*' both null, never zero

onet_education.name: O*NET 30.3 database — Occupation Data, Job Zones, Job Zone Reference, Education, Education Categories
onet_education.agency: U.S. Department of Labor / Employment and Training Administration (CC BY 4.0 — attribution printed on the page)

filters.element: 2.D.1 Required Level of Education, scale RL
filters.bins: 1-2 HS or less; 3-5 some college/associate; 6-7 bachelor's; 8-12 graduate
filters.join: .00 variant preferred, else equal-weight mean of variants; broad SOC 51-2090 = mean of five-char stem
filters.job_zone: 30.x reports zones 1 and 2 as one band keyed 2; a zone-1 row reads the merged reference row
filters.attribution: required on the page — printed in the education source line

nem.name: BLS Employment Projections, National Employment Matrix, industry to occupation

filters.industry: 326000 plastics and rubber products manufacturing (325000, 326100, 326200 also fetched)
filters.rows: Line Item detailed occupations only; Summary rows excluded
filters.geography: NATIONAL ONLY — no state or metro cut exists; any regional count built from it is a synthetic estimate under a stated assumption, and the sentence says so

odjfs.name: Ohio LMI long-term employment projections, 2022–2032
odjfs.agency: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services, Bureau of Labor Market Information

filters.geography: JobsOhio Northeast (18 counties, superset of PIC-12) and the four MSAs; Ashtabula and Wayne appear only in region and state figures
filters.row: one industry or one SOC occupation × geography: 2022 base, 2032 projected, change, percent, annual openings split, median wage
filters.projection_not_forecast: a modelled path with no confidence band; historically under-calls turning points
filters.register_cannot_be_rebuilt: 3252 is published only inside bundle 3250A1 and 3255 only inside 3250A2; only 326/3261/3262 are clean
